- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.3) mid-period, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit increase.
- Model exhibits strong lag in responding to sentiment shifts; if sentiment rises after day 5, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days unless sentiment >0.6.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+3σ above 30-day mean, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish; if below -3σ, increase by 5–10% unless sentiment bearish.
- For 30-day horizon, model underpredicts volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.0% volatility buffer if sentiment >0.4 for 3+ consecutive days.
